fullDesc: In the Dutch Republic of the 1630s, prices for rare tulip bulbs rose sharply and then crashed in February 1637. It is often cited as the first speculative bubble, though historians argue about how big it really was.
realFacts: Some bulbs sold for the price of a house, by the traditional story
Contracts for future delivery drove trading
The economic damage may have been smaller than the legend
The word tulip mania is still used for bubbles
